current_evidence: The council's 'Apply for planning permission' page still links this FULL guidance ('To be used for all applications excluding discharge of conditions...') alongside a separate 'Validation Guidance (Householder) 2026 Update'; the FULL document's cover reads 'Guidance Notes for Validation of Planning Applications March 2022' and no newer full list was found.

issues.detail: List date 2023-02-01 is taken from the upload folder in the URL, not the document. The FULL guidance is dated March 2022 on its cover. The householder guidance, which Grokbot also used, is a separate document with its own newer date (cover 'Updated October 2026', inner pages 'Updated January 2024'). The workbook does not record it.

issues.grok_comment: Correct that List_date 2023-02-01 comes from the URL folder while the FULL guidance cover says "March 2022". But the householder guidance date is recorded: every householder row cites the 2026-10 householder PDF with doc_date 2026-10-01.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. Householder rows carry their own 2026 date. The FULL guidance date (March 2022) is still recorded wrongly.

issues.detail: Contaminated Land / Land Contamination Assessment is listed under Householder and Advertisement consent. The source explicitly EXCLUDES those types. Grokbot read the exclusion as an inclusion.
issues.evidence: Item 35: 'All applications (excluding Householders, Advertisement and Heritage) where...land is or may be contaminated'

issues.detail: All 18 rows taken from the Householder guidance (tree survey, site plan, daylight, DAS, ecology, FRA, floor plans, heritage, highways, landscaping, photos, planning statement, pre-app, roof plan, street scene, structural survey, sunlight) are copied unchanged under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The householder guidance does not cover prior approval or change of use. Ventilation/Extraction is also placed under prior approval, but source item 28 is a general local-list item for commercial cooking/fume uses, not a prior-approval requirement.
issues.evidence: Householder guidance: it does not apply to separate buildings, a separate dwelling, or 'changing a dwelling (or part of it) to other uses'; no mention of prior approval

issues.detail: About 25 FULL-guidance rows are tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', e.g. Affordable Housing, Air Quality, Transport Assessment, BNG, Ecology, Heads of Terms, Viability. Examples: FRA (1ha+ in FZ1 or any FZ2/3), Affordable Housing (10+ dwellings/0.5ha), Coal Mining Risk Assessment (all except householder), Statement of Conformity with SCI (all major). Lawful development cert '(none)' also ignores item 45.

issues.detail: Flood Risk Assessment, Drainage Strategy/SuDS and Sequential/Exception Test all share one garbled excerpt. It merges the Street Scene trigger ('Detailed applications for new dwellings and major employment site... Conservation Areas') with the FRA heading and is cut off at '1 hectare or'. The actual triggers are: FRA for 1ha+ in Flood Zone 1 or new development in Zones 2/3 (excluding first-floor-and-above extensions); SuDS for major applications; sequential test for certain development in Zones 2/3.
issues.evidence: Item 14 'Flood Risk Assessment, Sustainable Drainage and Sequential test'

issues.detail: Habitats Regulations Assessment row's trigger is drainage text about hydrological impacts, not the HRA trigger. The source requires HRA information where likely significant effects on European sites occur, and mitigation within the Cannock Chase SAC Zone of Influence. The EIA row's trigger is likewise about including a Coal Mining Risk Assessment in an ES, not EIA Schedule 1/2 thresholds (item 43).
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'The management of the proposed system should include appropriate assessment of the quantity and quality of hydrological...'; Grokbot EIA: '...it is suggested that the CMRA is included within the ES'

issues.detail: Mislabelled or fragment triggers in Full planning. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is the Lighting Assessment text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' both reuse the Construction Method Statement sentence; the CEMP trigger in item 25a is residential >10 units or 0.4ha+, and commercial 1,000 sqm+ or 1ha+. 'Open space' is a table-of-contents line with dot leaders. 'Housing mix' is just 'Housing and Housing Mix SPD 16.' when the trigger is all major residential. 'BNG' is '(see 24b Biodiversity Net Gain)'; the item is actually 25b and applies to any net loss of habitat. 'Ecological Survey' is NatureSpace contact details. 'Arboricultural' begins with the stray heading 'Foul and Surface Water Drainage Assessment'.
issues.evidence: Grokbot Open space trigger: 'Applications affecting playing field land ......... 46 7 National List Validation Item...'

issues.detail: Householder rows from the 2026 householder guidance have wrong or irrelevant triggers. Landscaping uses fee text for amendment requests. Site levels/sections uses flood floor-level text; the source trigger is earthworks or a noticeable slope. Pre-application advice uses listed-building-consent text. Street scene is the fragment 'within the street scene.'. Planning statement says 'not needed', omitting that one is required where Green Belt/Open Countryside extension limits are exceeded. Photographs omits its trigger (demolition, conservation area, listed building). Flood Risk Assessment omits the Flood Zone 2/3 floor-level requirement.
issues.evidence: Grokbot Landscaping trigger: '...a minor alteration, such as a repositioned window or reduced roof height you will need to pay a further fee per request.'

issues.detail: Missing thresholds. The Air Quality excerpt does not name the four AQMAs (Penkridge, Essington, Wedges Mills, Hatherton). The Fire Statement excerpt omits the 18m / 7 storeys threshold for buildings with more than one dwelling. The Transport Assessment excerpt is mostly a phone number with no threshold.
issues.evidence: Fire statement: 'Full applications involving buildings which contain more than 1 dwelling... 18 metres or more in height or 7 or more storeys'

issues.detail: The two Cannock Chase SAC payment items are presented as 'currently £232' and 'will be £290.58' without stating which zone each applies to. The source applies £232/dwelling to the 0-8km zone and £290.58/dwelling to the 15km Zone of Influence for applications determined on or after 1 April 2022. The draft unilateral agreement text is also merged with a URL fragment ('22 nnock%20Chase%20SAC...').
issues.evidence: Item 18 Cannock Chase SAC / Draft Unilateral Undertaking

issues.detail: Several 'Submission rules' / policy tab items are process text or fragments, not validation requirements. These are: paper-copy numbers, hand-signed certificates, the definitive-map link sentence, 'You can attach electronic copies of your drawings...', the SAC payment amounts (fees), and the 'Special Protection Area (SPA)... 1b Nationally Designated Sites... 54 1c...' fragment, which is a table extract with a page number.
issues.evidence: Grokbot tab item: 'Special Protection Area (SPA) and Potential Special Protection Areas 1b Nationally Designated Sites ... 54 1c Regionally and Locally Designated Sites...'

issues.detail: The 'linear scale bar ... with written dimensions of the proposed works' text is captured twice in Drawing standards: once as a standalone item and once embedded in the cross-sections item.

summary: Grokbot's link is the FULL validation guidance the council still links, but the document is dated March 2022, not February 2023. The extraction is poor: many local items are missing (Coal Mining, Noise, SCI conformity, Agricultural need, Employment land, etc.), triggers are garbled or mislabelled, contaminated land is placed under the very types it excludes, and householder rows are wrongly copied to prior approval.
